Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are prepared to resolve this with meaningful payments to all identified members, without requiring claims. Our proposal provides a $32 million class fund and a separately paid fee subject to court approval. Any fee reduction would benefit the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that identified members should receive payments automatically and that any fee reduction should benefit the class. We can offer a $28 million class fund and $6 million in fees, subject to court approval, without clear sailing.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your agreement on automatic payments and directing any fee reduction to the class. We can narrow the gap with a $30 million class fund and $6 million in fees, subject to court approval, with the other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement and agree on automatic distribution and the fee terms. We can narrow the remaining gap with a $29 million class fund and $6 million in fees, subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept your latest term sheet: a $29 million class fund distributed automatically, with $6 million in separately paid fees subject to court approval, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fees going to the class.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial automatic-distribution fund and a separately stated, court-approved fee. Avoid fee reversion and clear sailing, which could undermine class interests and settlement approval.

The $39 million proposal is within authority and has court-friendly terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Counter with automatic payments and no fee reversion to preserve approval prospects.

The defense offer provides substantial, automatic class recovery and a court-approved fee, but there is room to negotiate a higher class fund. A modest counter preserves the distribution protections and avoids trading class recovery for fees.

Their $36 million proposal is within authority and uses court-approval-friendly terms. With four rounds remaining, a modest counteroffer may reduce Brightline's total outlay without sacrificing automatic payments or the fee protections.

The $29 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million trial-value estimate before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The separately paid $6 million fee remains subject to court approval, and any reduction benefits the class. Accepting serves the class's interests.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: As interim class counsel, I submit this statement in support of preliminary approval. The parties negotiated the class fund and attorneys’ fees together from the first exchange of proposals; fees were not deferred until after class relief was agreed. Counsel initially proposed a $32 million class fund and $7 million in separately paid fees. Brightline countered with $28 million and $6 million, respectively. Counsel then proposed a $30 million fund with $6 million in fees, and accepted Brightline’s counterproposal of a $29 million fund with $6 million in fees. Throughout these exchanges, both sides agreed that payments would be automatic, without a claims process; Brightline would not receive any unawarded fees; and there would be no clear-sailing agreement. The $6 million fee remains subject to court approval, and any reduction will go to the class.
